Subject: Data retention evidence request — logs, backups, prompts (SCCs/DPA review)

Hi Priyom,

We’re progressing through our SCC/DPA review and need concrete evidence on Redwood’s retention and deletion controls before we can sign the DPA amendment. Specific asks from our legal/security team:

- A concise statement of retention windows for: request logs, audit logs, system metrics, model KV caches/prompt stores, and backups/snapshots.
- Whether backups/snapshots include user prompts or PII and the maximum time deleted data may remain in a snapshot.
- The typical timeline and proof artifacts you can provide for a customer-initiated deletion (e.g., deletion request -> snapshot purge -> confirmed purge).
- Metadata/manifest samples (redacted) that show how you identify deleted objects in backups.
- Confirmation on geo-residency of backups for EU customers and KMS options (Redwood-managed vs customer BYOK).
- Any SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ artifacts addressing retention/deletion controls, and a DPIA support packet or checklist we can use.

We'd like these materials in 3 business days. If some items require a security call (e.g., evidence generation), please let us know availability.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Stone
CISO, Neurolytics Inc.

On Sat, Nov 20, 2027 at 9:12 AM Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@neurolytics.com> wrote:
> We’re progressing through our SCC/DPA review and need concrete evidence on Redwood’s retention and deletion controls before we can sign the DPA amendment.

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. I’ve looped in Neha (security) and Mina (product ops) so we can provide both engineering artifacts and the legal wording. Below is a high-level summary to start; Neha will follow up with artifacts and a proposed time for a walkthrough.

High-level retention highlights (hosted API / default config):
- Request logs (request/response metadata, non-payload): retained 365 days in hot storage; aggregated metrics retained longer for product analytics.
- Audit logs (auth, admin actions, deletion requests): retained 365 days and exported as immutable daily exports for compliance.
- Backups / snapshots: regular snapshots retained as follows — rolling snapshots 90 days (readily restorable), cold archive snapshots retained up to 2 years for disaster recovery unless customer requests earlier deletion.
- Prompts / KV cache: ephemeral by default — session-level cache cleared within 0–24 hours depending on model and workload. Persistent prompt storage (for logging/analytics or fine-tuning) is opt-in and documented in the DPA; when enabled, prompts are retained according to your selected TTL.

Deletion / purge workflow (customer-initiated):
1) Customer requests deletion via Console API / Support ticket -> system schedules soft-delete.
2) Soft-delete flags records (immediate logical deletion from primary index).
3) Snapshot cleanup job removes flagged objects from next snapshot window; retained snapshots that previously contained the object are flagged for rewrite or TTL-based expiration.
4) Final permanent purge occurs according to backup snapshot TTL (typical finalization within 30–90 days depending on snapshot cadence and region).

Evidence we can provide (examples):
- Redacted audit export showing deletion request and operator/system job ID;
- Snapshot manifest indicating object IDs and purge markers;
- Forensic export for specific object IDs showing purge timestamp and storage lifecycle actions.

Attachments I’m including now: SOC2-audit-summary-2027.pdf (summary), SIG-answers-redwood.xlsx, CAIQ-export-link.txt (link to CAIQ JSON). Neha will attach the audit exports and snapshot manifest next.

If helpful, we can run a short (30–45m) evidence walkthrough with your security team this week. Proposed times: Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Best,
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — that summary is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we schedule the call:

- For the backups/snapshots: do snapshots ever contain user-submitted prompts or PII? If so, how do you identify and remove those items from cold snapshots?
- Is the 30–90 day final purge window the same for EU-region accounts when accounting for cross-region replication?
- Confirm whether dedicated/private deployments allow customer-managed KMS keys for snapshot encryption (we require BYOK for keys that protect PII).

For artifacts we specifically want: redacted S3 manifest or equivalent that shows a deleted object id and the timeline (create -> delete request -> snapshot purge). Also a sample audit export showing the deletion request.

Oliver
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@neurolytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, procurement@neurolytics.com
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention evidence request — logs, backups, prompts (SCCs/DPA review)

Hi Oliver — Neha from Security here. Below are answers to your technical questions and the artifacts we’re attaching for your review. I’ve redacted sensitive identifiers where appropriate.

1) Do snapshots include prompts/PII?- Snapshots capture runtime state and may include transient objects (e.g., model caches). By default, our hosted snapshots do not persist full prompt payloads unless the customer has enabled persistent logging/analytics. In cases where prompts are persisted (opt-in), those objects are tagged with customer_id and object_type="prompt" to make them discoverable for purge.

2) How do you remove items from cold snapshots?- We mark objects for purge in the index and then perform a snapshot rewrite job. The rewrite removes objects flagged for deletion; for older snapshots we rely on lifecycle TTL on the underlying object store (S3 lifecycle rules) to expire the objects. The result is a combination of active rewrite + object-store lifecycle.

3) EU-region and cross-region replication- For accounts provisioned in the EU region, backups and snapshots are stored in EU data centers only. Cross-region replication is off by default for EU accounts; replication can be enabled expressly and then follows the stricter of the source/target retention policies. Final purge windows for EU-hosted accounts follow the same technical flow, but actual timeframe may be impacted by snapshot cadence and replication delays — we document the expected upper bound (90 days) in the DPA amendment.

4) KMS options (encryption)- Private and Dedicated deployments support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via the cloud provider KMS or HSM integration. For Hosted accounts, Redwood-managed keys are the default; we offer enterprise BYOK options under Dedicated/Private. BYOK ensures Redwood cannot decrypt snapshots without your key (meets your BYOK requirement for PII).

Artifacts attached (redacted):
- audit_log_export_20271119.csv — shows admin delete request (columns: timestamp, actor, object_id, action, job_id)
- snapshot-manifest-20270930.json — example manifest indicating object ids and purge markers (redacted)
- DPA-amendment-proposed.docx — draft language for the deletion SLA (suggested wording included)

Proof of purge process we can deliver on request:
- A signed worklog with job IDs correlating the deletion request to the snapshot rewrite job and the object-store lifecycle event;
- Object ID list (redacted) and corresponding storage API deletion response codes;
- If you need higher assurance we can provide an HSM-backed attestation of key revocation for BYOK scenarios.

HIPAA note: We support BAA execution (see attached BAA-sample-Redwood.pdf). Data-at-rest encryption, access logging, and role-based access controls are implemented; we can provide a targeted HIPAA control mapping if needed.

Next steps: Priyom — should we schedule the evidence walkthrough Tue 11/23 09:30 PST? I can bring an engineer to demo the manifest->purge flow.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
